findings.title: Dynamic imports are executed eagerly instead of lazily
findings.body: Every value in the appStore object is created by immediately calling import(), so merely importing appStore starts loading all 29 app modules, including apps unrelated to the current request. This defeats the intended lazy/code-split loading, adds startup and module-evaluation cost to every consumer of getCalendar, videoClient, and payment code, and creates rejected promises for unused apps that may surface as unhandled rejections if a module fails to load. Store loader functions such as () => import('./applecalendar') and invoke them at call sites, or provide an async getter.

findings.title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) discards the callback promises. Now that getCalendar must be awaited, deleteEvent/deleteMeeting are not even invoked before the function sends the reschedule email and returns true; in a short-lived/serverless invocation they can be dropped, and any rejection becomes an unhandled rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch, which only catches synchronous errors. Replace forEach with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) so deletions complete and failures are logged.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar/video deletions
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) discards the callback promises. After this change the callbacks suspend at await getCalendar, while the mutation immediately proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks and can finish before the old calendar/video events are deleted, leaving orphan events that keep the old time busy; failures are also unhandled rejections. Use await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) before sending the email/returning.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race past apiDeletes collection
findings.body: In the allRemainingBookings recurring branch, credentials are processed with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }). Those callbacks suspend at the await, so when line 652 later evaluates Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)), concat snapshots an apiDeletes array that does not yet contain the calendar deletions. The handler can therefore delete attendees/booking references and return while recurring calendar events are still present or never deleted, and deletion errors are unhandled. Replace the async forEach with a for...of loop or await Promise.all(...map(...)) that populates apiDeletes before it is awaited.
